requirements.heading: Aggregate Reports
requirements.text: A separate report MUST be generated for each DMARC Policy Domain encountered during the reporting period.

requirements.heading: Aggregate Reports
requirements.text: Each report MUST contain data for only one DMARC Policy Domain.

requirements.heading: Aggregate Reports
requirements.text: A single report MUST contain data for one policy configuration.

requirements.heading: Aggregate Reports
requirements.text: If multiple configurations were observed during a single reporting period, a reporting entity MAY choose to send multiple reports; otherwise, the reporting entity SHOULD note only the final configuration observed during the period.

requirements.heading: Description of the Content of the XML File
requirements.text: If a document does not match the specified format, the document evaluator SHOULD discard the report.

requirements.heading: Description of the Content of the XML File
requirements.text: The evaluator MAY choose to try to utilize some of the data; however, if the format is in question, the data may be as well.

requirements.heading: Description of the Content of the XML File
requirements.text: The report evaluator MAY choose to contact the report generator so that they may be alerted to an issue with the report format.

requirements.heading: Description of the Content of the XML File
requirements.text: O: OPTIONAL, zero or one element

requirements.heading: Description of the Content of the XML File
requirements.text: R: REQUIRED, exactly one element

requirements.heading: Description of the Content of the XML File
requirements.text: *: OPTIONAL, zero or more elements

requirements.heading: Description of the Content of the XML File
requirements.text: +: REQUIRED, one or more elements

requirements.heading: First Level Elements
requirements.text: The elements in this table MUST appear in the order listed.

requirements.heading: First Level Elements
requirements.text: There MUST be at least one "record" element; these elements contain data stating that IP addresses were seen to have delivered messages for the Author Domain to the receiving system.

requirements.heading: Contents of the "date_range" Element
requirements.text: When generating reports, these reporting periods SHOULD NOT overlap.

requirements.heading: Contents of the "extension" Element
requirements.text: These elements MUST be namespaced.

requirements.heading: Contents of the "record" Element
requirements.text: The report MUST contain one or more records stating which IP addresses were seen to have delivered messages for the Author Domain to the receiving system.

requirements.heading: Contents of the "record" Element
requirements.text: Use of extensions may cause other elements to be added to the end of the record; such elements MUST be namespaced.

requirements.heading: Contents of the "policy_evaluated" Element
requirements.text: If alignment fails and the policy applied does not match the DMARC Policy Domain's configured policy, the "reason" element MUST be included.

requirements.heading: Contents of the "policy_evaluated" Element
requirements.text: * "spf" and "dkim" MUST be the evaluated values as they relate to DMARC, not the values the receiver may have used when overriding the policy.

requirements.heading: Contents of the "identifiers" Element
requirements.text: * "envelope_from" MAY exist but be empty if the message had a null reverse-path (see Section 4.5.5 of [RFC5321]).

requirements.heading: Contents of the "auth_results" Element
requirements.text: If validation is attempted for any DKIM signature, the results MUST be included in the report (within reason; see Section 3.1.3 ("DKIM Signatures in Aggregate Reports") below for handling numerous signatures).

requirements.heading: Handling Domains in Reports
requirements.text: In the same report, there MUST be a single DMARC Policy Domain, though there could be multiple RFC5322.From domains.

requirements.heading: DKIM Signatures in Aggregate Reports
requirements.text: A report SHOULD contain no more than 100 signatures for a given "row", in decreasing priority.

requirements.heading: Unique Identifiers in Aggregate Reporting
requirements.text: These are the fields that MUST be identical when used.

requirements.text: The "type" element MUST have one of the pre-defined values listed below.

requirements.heading: Extensions
requirements.text: The absence or existence of this section SHOULD NOT create an error when processing reports.

requirements.heading: Report Delivery
requirements.text: The Mail Receiver, after preparing a report, MUST evaluate the provided reporting URIs (see [RFC9989]) in the order given.

requirements.heading: Report Delivery
requirements.text: If any of the URIs are malformed, they SHOULD be ignored.

requirements.heading: Report Delivery
requirements.text: An attempt MUST be made to deliver an aggregate report to every remaining URI, up to the Receiver's limits on supported URIs.

requirements.heading: Report Delivery
requirements.text: If delivery is not possible because the services advertised by the published URIs are not able to accept reports (e.g., the URI refers to a service that is unreachable), the Mail Receiver MAY cache that data and try again later or MAY discard data that could not be sent.

requirements.heading: Report Delivery
requirements.text: Where the URI specified in a "rua" tag does not specify otherwise, a Mail Receiver generating a feedback report SHOULD employ a secure transport mechanism, meaning the report should be delivered over a channel employing TLS (SMTP+STARTTLS).

requirements.heading: Definition of Report-ID
requirements.text: This identifier MUST be unique among reports to the same domain to aid receivers in identifying duplicate reports should they happen.

requirements.heading: Email
requirements.text: The message generated by the Mail Receiver MUST be as described in [RFC5322] and formatted per [RFC2045].

requirements.heading: Email
requirements.text: The aggregate report itself MUST be included in one of the parts of the message, as an attachment with a corresponding media type from below.

requirements.heading: Email
requirements.text: A human-readable annotation MAY be included as a body part (with a human-friendly content-type, such as "text/plain" or "text/html").

requirements.heading: Email
requirements.text: The aggregate data MUST be an XML file that SHOULD be subjected to GZIP [RFC1952] compression.

requirements.heading: Email
requirements.text: The aggregate data MUST be present using the media type "application/gzip" if compressed (see [RFC6713]) and "text/xml" otherwise.

requirements.heading: Email
requirements.text: The attachment filename MUST be constructed using the following ABNF:

requirements.heading: Email
requirements.text: The extension MUST be "xml" for a plain XML file or "xml.gz" for an XML file compressed using GZIP.

requirements.heading: Email
requirements.text: If a report generator needs to re-send a report, the system MUST use the same filename as the original report.

requirements.heading: Email
requirements.text: Mail streams carrying DMARC feedback data MUST conform to the DMARC mechanism, thereby resulting in an aligned "pass" (see Section 4.4 of [RFC9989]).

requirements.heading: Email
requirements.text: Optionally, the report sender MAY choose to use the same "ridtxt" as a part or whole of the RFC5322.Message-Id header included with the report.

requirements.heading: Handling of Duplicates
requirements.text: As noted above, the sender MUST use the same unique identifiers when sending the report.

requirements.heading: Verifying External Destinations
requirements.text: When a Mail Receiver discovers a DMARC Policy Record in the DNS, and the Organizational Domain at which that record was discovered is not identical to the Organizational Domain of the host part of the authority component of a [RFC3986] specified in the "rua" tag, the following verification steps MUST be taken:

requirements.heading: Verifying External Destinations
requirements.text: If the result of this request is a temporary DNS error of some kind (e.g., a timeout), the Mail Receiver MAY elect to temporarily fail the delivery so the verification test can be repeated later.

requirements.heading: Verifying External Destinations
requirements.text: In particular, the "v=DMARC1" tag is mandatory and MUST appear first in the list.

requirements.heading: Verifying External Destinations
requirements.text: However, to prevent loops or indirect abuse, the overriding URI MUST use the same destination host from the first step.

requirements.heading: Verifying External Destinations
requirements.text: Where the above algorithm fails to confirm that the external reporting was authorized by the Report Consumer, the URI MUST be ignored by the Mail Receiver generating the report.

requirements.heading: Verifying External Destinations
requirements.text: Further, if the confirming record includes a URI whose host is again different than the domain publishing that override, the Mail Receiver generating the report MUST NOT generate a report to either the original or the override URI.

requirements.heading: Extensible Reporting
requirements.text: These extensions MUST be properly formatted XML and meant to exist within the structure of a DMARC report.

requirements.heading: Extensible Reporting
requirements.text: In either case, the extensions MUST contain a URI to the definition of the extension so that the receiver understands how to interpret the data.

requirements.heading: Extensible Reporting
requirements.text: If a processor is unable to handle an extension in a report, it SHOULD ignore the data and continue to the next extension.

requirements.heading: Feedback Leakage
requirements.text: To minimize this potential concern, PSD DMARC feedback MUST be limited to aggregate reports.

requirements.heading: Informative References
requirements.text: If alignment fails and the policy applied does not match the domain's configured policy, the reason element MUST be specified.
